newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - Parallel bond sparks interest.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - Parallel bond sparks interest.

text.p: The Eurobond market this week was taking more interest in growing talk of an unprecedented parallel bond from Brazil, while Bradies look set for a bumpy ride on a slew of U.S. economic data, traders and analysts said.

EUROBOND PLAYERS hope to learn over the next few days which banks will lead manage Brazil's upcoming $450 million parallel bond. The bonds are called "parallel" because they carry the same maturity and coupon in a variety of currencies.
The deal will be fungible, or redenominated, to the euro currency after the introduction of the single European currency in 1999.

Central Bank international affairs director Gustavo Franco said over the weekend that Brazil was considering issuing $450 million in at least three of the following four currencies: French francs, marks, guilders or Austrian schillings.

Brazil missed its chance to be the first fungible bond issuer from Latin America when Argentina launched a fungible deal last week. Brazil, however, could still become the first emerging market parallel bond issuer.
"This is in line with the Central Bank's policy of issuing as little as possible, but making as much noise as possible," said Hans Ostlund, a director at West Merchant Bank in Brazil.
Bond origination desks in Brazil said a fair number of mandates for Eurobond deals were being negotiated, but the timing of the deals would depend on a more stable U.S. T-bond.

IN SECONDARY TRADE, Brazil's 8-7/8 percent global due 2001 ZQ4P outperformed most corporates last week, tightening to 184 basis points over U.S. Treasuries. The bond had been trading in the 210-220 bp range.

"There is a big spread differential between the Brazil global and corporates like Eletrobras and Cemig. The spread is now about 50 bps and historically it's around 15," said a Eurobond trader in Sao Paulo.
He said Eletrobas' 9-1/8 percent due 2004 (call 2001) ZUQU or Cemig's 9-1/8 pct due 2004 (call 2001) ZQRO, both trading at about 230 bps over, were attractive against the global.

THE BRADY MARKET will keep its eye on U.S. economic data, including consumer price inflation, industrial capacity and inventories. Anxiety over the numbers should keep the U.S. Treasury market off balance and sideline fixed-income investors, who are waiting for a clearer short-term outlook.
"Investors will be on the sidelines. They'll be some bottom-fishers, but not enough to drive the market," said Pedro Barbosa, head of Brady trading for ING Bank in Brazil.

C bonds BR8D14=RR were hit hard after Friday's downturn in the bond market and are trading at more than 500 bps over. Brazil debt watchers, many of whom see Cs trading in the 350 bp over range by year's end, say the bonds are attractive at this level.
But current market unease will block any dive into Cs, pars and other fixed-rate assets, players said.

"When people start swapping into fixed-rate Bradies from floaters, that will be a signal from the market that it thinks interest rates have stabilized," said a fixed-income analyst based in Sao Paulo.

Although external factors would continue to drive Brazilian prices of fixed-income assets abroad, debt watchers said they would monitor progress on the government's administrative reform bill in the lower house of Congress. A vote was expected by as early as Wednesday.
